Method-general analysis. The selection engine for the main analysis is set once via fs_subgroup_method in the setup chunk — "consistency" (default), "dina", or "grf" (with fs_grf_selection = "tree"/"frontier"). The headline fit and every downstream step — full bootstrap, Tier-2 de-biased gate, cross-validation, leave-one-out, and the subgroup outcome plot — inherit that engine from the single fitted object, so the whole analysis re-renders under a different method by changing one knob. The comparative DINA-screening, standalone-DINA, and GRF sections that follow are fixed illustrations of the individual engines and are unaffected by fs_subgroup_method.

This is the binary-outcome (odds-ratio) counterpart to the GBSG Cox multimethod vignette. Everything operates on a single adverse scale (y_binary_neg, the indicator of no CD4 improvement), so an OR above the screening threshold indicates harm — the direct analogue of an HR above the threshold on the survival path. The Tier-1 (full bootstrap) vs Tier-2 (fast multiplier-bootstrap de-biased gate) comparison is reported for each engine.

0.1 Parallel Processing Configuration

ForestSearch supports parallel processing for computationally intensive operations (bootstrap, cross-validation).

Show code 
# Detect available cores
n_cores_total <- parallel::detectCores()
n_cores <- max(1L, floor(0.80 * parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE)))
cat("Using", n_cores, "of", n_cores_total, "total cores for parallel processing")
#> Using 102 of 128 total cores for parallel processing
Show code 
# Number of bootstrap iterations
# Use 500-2000 for production; reduced here for demo / pressure test
NB <- 1000L

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Validation toggles (the slowest parts of the document).  Independent:
# run_cv  controls K-Fold cross-validation; run_loo controls leave-one-out
# (N-fold / OOB).  Either can be turned off without affecting the other.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
run_cv  <- FALSE    # K-Fold cross-validation (kfold-cv + diagnostics)
run_loo <- FALSE    # Leave-one-out / N-fold OOB (oob-cv)
# 10-fold CV with multiple iterations.  Use Ksims >= 50 for production.
Ksims <- 50L

# Pre-seed CV/LOO timings so the Computational Timing table is well-formed
# whether or not these run (skipped analyses report NA).
timings$kfold <- NA_real_
timings$oob   <- NA_real_

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Per-analysis identification parameters (tune each analysis independently).
#   sg_focus       : which candidate subgroup the selection step chooses
#   or_threshold   : harm floor on the OR scale (adverse scale: OR > c1 = harm)
#   or_consistency : minimum per-split consistency OR (consistency search only)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main ForestSearch (consistency search)
fs_sg_focus              <- "effMaxSG"   # GLM-natural alias of "hrMaxSG"
fs_selection_rule        <- "neighborhood"       # neighborhood ∩ Pareto (effMaxSG/effMinSG)
fs_or_threshold          <- 1.0
fs_or_consistency        <- 1.0
fs_pconsistency          <- 0.90
# IMPORTANT: the Tier-2 de-biased gate on the GLM path runs ONLY under the
# resample-consistency engine (consistency_method = "resample").  Under the
# default "split" engine the gate is silently skipped for GLM outcomes.
fs_consistency_method    <- "resample"
# Tier-2 de-biased gate: a fast multiplier-bootstrap approximation of the
# bootstrap bias-correction, computed inside the fit and compared to the full
# bootstrap below.  It runs for whichever selection engine fs_subgroup_method
# names, de-biasing against that engine's own candidate family (it re-derives
# the per-candidate GLM dfbeta itself).
run_mr <- TRUE     # add mr_inference = TRUE to the forestsearch call
mr_draws      <- 5000L    # multiplier-bootstrap draws for the gate

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output location for this document's results:  <base>/<dirout>/
#   results_dir = NULL -> base is <qmd dir>/_payloads
#   dirout      = NULL -> the .qmd stem
# Setting results_dir redirects the base only; each run still gets its own
# subdirectory named by dirout.
#
# Examples:
#   results_dir <- NULL;  dirout <- NULL
#     -> <qmd dir>/_payloads/<stem>/<stem>_payload.rds
#   results_dir <- NULL;  dirout <- "gbsg_survival_multimethod"
#     -> <qmd dir>/_payloads/gbsg_survival_multimethod/gbsg_survival_multimethod_payload.rds
#   results_dir <- "~/GitHub/fs-post-selection-manuscript_jasa/_payloads"; dirout <- NULL
#     -> ~/GitHub/fs-post-selection-manuscript_jasa/_payloads/<stem>/<stem>_payload.rds
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
results_dir <- NULL
dirout      <- NULL

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# FIXED-FAMILY CONFIGURATION (use_lasso = FALSE, use_grf = FALSE)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fully enumerated candidate family: no LASSO or GRF screening, and as of
# 2026-08 no max_subgroups_search truncation.
#
# This is the fixed-family configuration the method's Theorem 1 certifies:
# the family is enumerated (default cuts, with J = 10 cuts for wtkg and
# cd40) rather than model-screened, so the bias correction captures all
# selection optimism.
#
# The published supplement Table S11 ({wtkg>86} & {cd40>380}, n=72,
# naive OR 3.58, FB 2.43, MR 1.80) came from an earlier run of this document
# that capped candidate evaluation at 50 (max_subgroups_search = 50L). That
# cap has been removed so the analysis follows the recommended specification
# rather than the earlier run. Results may therefore differ from the
# published table; the difference is intentional.
#
# Prior run (superseded): payload built 2026-07-08 on the 128-core machine,
# 5000 MR draws, max_subgroups_search = 50L.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Selection engine for the MAIN analysis.  The headline fit, its bootstrap,
# the de-biased gate, CV/LOO, and the subgroup outcome plot all flow from this
# single fit, so flipping subgroup_method re-runs the entire main analysis
# under that engine (each downstream step inherits the method from the fitted
# object):
#   "consistency" - the splitting-consistency search (default);
#   "dina"        - DINA performs selection (consistency search bypassed);
#   "grf"         - GRF performs selection (policy tree or DR-frontier).
# The Tier-2 gate de-biases against whichever engine's OWN candidate family,
# with re-selection matching that engine's selection rule.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
fs_subgroup_method <- "consistency"  # "consistency" | "dina" | "grf"
fs_grf_selection   <- "frontier"     # only if subgroup_method == "grf": "tree" | "frontier"
fs_grf_select_statistic <- "effect"  # only if subgroup_method=="grf" & grf_selection=="frontier": "dr" | "effect".
                                     #   "dr"     = native DR-score frontier winner;
                                     #   "effect" = re-rank the DR frontier on the inferential GLM OR (the
                                     #              statistic the Tier-2 gate de-biases).  No-op for the policy tree.
fs_grf_depth       <- 2L             # GRF depth (screening + GRF selection)
fs_dmin_grf        <- 0              # GRF DR-score screening floor (RD scale for binary; 0 = permissive)
fs_dina_args       <- list()         # extra args forwarded to DINA selection
fs_dina_select_statistic <- "effect" # only if subgroup_method=="dina": "dina" | "effect".
                                     #   "dina"   = native DINA tau-hat winner;
                                     #   "effect" = re-rank the DINA family on the inferential GLM OR (the
                                     #              statistic the Tier-2 gate de-biases).
# Tier-2 gate (main analysis): the gate's re-selection family for "dina"/"grf" is
# restricted to candidates competitive on the method's NATIVE statistic (DINA
# tau-hat / GRF DR-score).  NULL = use the recommended default, which matches the
# band to effect_neighborhood automatically (the band the engine selects within);
# give a number in (0, 1) to set the band explicitly, or >= 1 to de-bias against
# the full family.  Ignored for "consistency" (its maxcons re-selection already
# matches the search).
fs_family_native_nbhd <- NULL

# (A) ForestSearch + DINA screening (consistency search selects; DINA only
#     contributes candidate cuts)
dina_screen_sg_focus             <- "effMaxSG"
dina_screen_or_threshold         <- 1.0
dina_screen_or_consistency       <- 0.9
# Screening cut set: FALSE => full DINA frontier; TRUE => only the single
# dina_subgroup()-selected cut (uses dina_screen_sg_focus / selection_rule).
dina_screen_selected_only        <- TRUE

# (C) ForestSearch subgroup_method = "dina" (DINA performs selection; the
#     consistency search is bypassed, so or_consistency does not apply here).
#     The standalone DINA analysis (B) reuses these so (B) and (C) match.
fs_dina_sg_focus     <- "effMaxSG"
fs_dina_or_threshold <- 1.0
# Tier-2 gate: the DINA re-selection family is restricted to candidates competitive
# on DINA's native tau-hat.  NULL = recommended default (matches effect_neighborhood
# automatically); set a number in (0, 1) for an explicit band, or >= 1 for the full
# family.  Note: this only tunes candidate competition -- the gate holds the forest
# fixed, so the full bootstrap stays the reference for DINA regardless.
fs_dina_family_native_nbhd <- NULL

# (D) ForestSearch subgroup_method = "grf" (GRF performs selection via a causal
#     forest policy tree or DR-score frontier; the consistency search, LASSO and
#     DINA are bypassed).  Dedicated demo: always runs GRF regardless of
#     fs_subgroup_method, mirroring the standalone DINA selection (C).
fs_grf_demo_selection     <- "frontier"  # "frontier" | "tree"
fs_grf_demo_depth         <- 2L          # GRF tree / DR-pair depth
fs_grf_demo_dmin          <- 0.0         # DR-score harm floor (RD scale; 0 = permissive default)
fs_grf_sg_focus           <- "effMaxSG"  # -> GRF frontier/tree selection rule
# Tier-2 gate: the GRF re-selection family is restricted to candidates competitive
# on GRF's native (RD-based) DR-score.  NULL = recommended default (matches
# effect_neighborhood automatically); set a number in (0, 1) for an explicit band,
# or >= 1 for the full family.  Note: this only tunes candidate competition -- the
# gate holds the forest fixed, so the full bootstrap stays the reference for GRF
# regardless (a dominant DR-score winner can collapse the family to 1).
fs_grf_family_native_nbhd <- NULL

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Numeric precision (two-stage control).
#   construction_digits : upstream sprintf precision in the bootstrap / CV
#     table builders.  Acts as a CEILING for downstream display.
#   display_digits      : precision rendered in user-facing tables.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
construction_digits <- 2L
display_digits      <- 2L

# Display-only tidy of a subgroup label for printing: rounds the post-operator
# thresholds to `d` decimals via the package's tidy_cut_display().  The
# membership-exact sg.harm (re-parsed by get_dfpred and carried through the
# bootstrap) is never altered -- this only affects what is printed.  Used at
# every site in this document that renders sg.harm.
fmt_sg <- function(x, d = display_digits) {
  if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0L) return(x)
  paste(forestsearch:::tidy_cut_display(x, digits = as.integer(d)), collapse = " & ")
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pareto-frontier diagnostic parameters (drives compute_frontier_cis(),
# plot_pareto_frontier(), pareto_frontier_table(), explain_pareto_selection()).
# For OR (ratio-scale), the effect axis is auto-rendered on log scale.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
frontier_params <- list(
  n_splits      = 1000L,
  seed          = 1L,
  xlim          = c(0.35, 10),   # OR auto-detected as ratio scale
  digits        = 2L
)

1 Introduction

This vignette demonstrates the ForestSearch methodology for exploratory subgroup identification with a binary outcome on the odds-ratio (OR) scale, applied to the ACTG175 trial. It uses the GLM extension of ForestSearch (León et al. 2024 Statistics in Medicine) and is the binary-outcome counterpart to the GBSG Cox multimethod analysis.

1.1 Motivation

In clinical trials, particularly oncology and infectious-disease studies, subgroup analyses are essential for:

  • Evaluating treatment effect consistency across patient populations
  • Identifying subgroups where treatment may be detrimental (harm)
  • Characterizing subgroups with enhanced benefit
  • Informing regulatory decisions and clinical practice

While prespecified subgroups provide stronger evidence, important subgroups based on patient characteristics may not be anticipated. ForestSearch provides a principled approach to exploratory subgroup identification with proper statistical inference.

1.2 Methodology Overview

ForestSearch identifies subgroups through:

  1. Candidate factor selection: Using LASSO and/or Generalized Random Forests (GRF)
  2. Exhaustive subgroup search: Evaluating all combinations up to maxk factors
  3. Consistency-based selection: Applying splitting consistency criteria
  4. Bootstrap bias correction: Adjusting for selection-induced optimism
  5. Cross-validation: Assessing algorithm stability

The key innovation is the splitting consistency criterion: a subgroup is considered “consistent with harm” if, when randomly split 50/50 many times, both halves consistently show odds ratios at or above the harm threshold (for example, 1.0 representing a nominal “harm” boundary on the adverse scale).

1.3 Single-Scale (Adverse) Framing

Note

ForestSearch and threshold direction. ForestSearch was developed for survival data where the outcome is typically the timing of an adverse event and thresholds (e.g., indicative of harm) are defined on the hazard-ratio scale. For a binary endpoint, the same harm logic applies on the adverse scale: the outcome y_binary_neg = 1 - y_binary_pos is the indicator of no CD4 improvement (1 = worse), and with adverse_outcome = TRUE an OR above the screening threshold means the treatment increases the odds of no improvement (harm). This is the direct binary analogue of an HR above the threshold on the survival path, so the entire multimethod workflow — consistency, DINA, and GRF — runs on this one scale.

1.4 Trial Background

ACTG175 (Hammer et al. 1996) randomized HIV-positive patients with CD4 counts of 200–500 per mm³ to four treatment arms. This analysis uses the two pure-monotherapy/combination arms:

  • Arm 1: ZDV + ddI combination therapy (treatment, T = 1)
  • Arm 3: ddI monotherapy (control, T = 0)

The outcome is the change in CD4 count from baseline to week 20 (cd40 → cd420), dichotomized into the improvement indicator.

3 Data: ACTG175 Trial

3.1 Treatment Assignment

Show code 
# ACTG175: arm 1 = ZDV+ddI (experimental), arm 3 = ddI (control)
actg_df <- subset(speff2trial::ACTG175, arms %in% c(1L, 3L))
actg_df$id <- seq_len(nrow(actg_df))

# Treatment: ZDV+ddI = 1, ddI = 0 (no switching)
actg_df$treat <- ifelse(actg_df$arms == 1L, 1L, 0L)

3.2 Outcome Construction

Show code 
# Drop subjects missing the week-20 CD4 measurement
actg_df <- actg_df[!is.na(actg_df$cd420), ]

# Beneficial scale: CD4 improvement indicator (1 = improved, higher = better)
actg_df$y_binary_pos <- as.integer(actg_df$cd420 > actg_df$cd40)

# Adverse scale: NO improvement indicator (1 = did not improve, higher = worse).
# This is the single analysis scale for the entire multimethod workflow.
actg_df$y_binary_neg <- 1L - actg_df$y_binary_pos

cat("Sample size:", nrow(actg_df), "\n")
#> Sample size: 1083
Show code 
cat("Adverse events (no improvement):", sum(actg_df$y_binary_neg),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * mean(actg_df$y_binary_neg)))
#> Adverse events (no improvement): 430 (39.7%)
Show code 
cat("Baseline factors:", paste(confounders.name, collapse = ", "), "\n")
#> Baseline factors: age, preanti, wtkg, karnof, cd40, cd80, hemo, homo, drugs, race, gender, symptom

3.3 Covariates

Show code 
# Keep ALL candidate covariates numeric.  forestsearch() builds and evaluates
# "var <= value" candidate cuts, and its DINA paths require numeric columns, so
# binary indicators left as factors trigger hundreds of "'<=' not meaningful for
# factors" warnings during the consistency search and "covariate must be numeric"
# failures in DINA (both subgroup_method = "dina" selection and use_dina
# screening).  With 0/1 numeric coding, forestsearch's cont.cutoff (= 4 unique
# values) treats the binary candidates as categorical automatically -- no factor
# conversion is needed, and every engine (consistency, DINA, GRF, standalone
# DINA) receives numeric covariates.
for (v in bin_vars) actg_df[[v]] <- as.numeric(actg_df[[v]])

cat("Continuous candidates:", paste(cont_vars, collapse = ", "), "\n")
#> Continuous candidates: age, preanti, wtkg, karnof, cd40, cd80
Show code 
cat("Binary candidates:    ", paste(bin_vars, collapse = ", "), "\n")
#> Binary candidates:     hemo, homo, drugs, race, gender, symptom

3.5 ITT Analysis (Adverse Scale)

Show code 
# Adverse-scale ITT OR (y_binary_neg = no improvement; OR > 1 = treatment
# increases the odds of no improvement = harm).
itt_neg <- glm(y_binary_neg ~ treat, data = actg_df, family = binomial)

beta  <- coef(itt_neg)["treat"]
se    <- summary(itt_neg)$coefficients["treat", "Std. Error"]
z     <- beta / se
p     <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(z))
itt_or    <- exp(beta)
itt_ci_lo <- exp(beta - qnorm(0.975) * se)
itt_ci_hi <- exp(beta + qnorm(0.975) * se)

cat("=== ITT Odds Ratio, adverse scale (y_binary_neg) ===\n")
#> === ITT Odds Ratio, adverse scale (y_binary_neg) ===
Show code 
cat(sprintf("  log-OR (treat): %7.4f  (SE %.4f)\n", beta, se))
#>   log-OR (treat): -0.4078  (SE 0.1252)
Show code 
cat(sprintf("  OR:             %6.3f  (95%% CI: %.3f, %.3f)\n",
            itt_or, itt_ci_lo, itt_ci_hi))
#>   OR:              0.665  (95% CI: 0.520, 0.850)
Show code 
cat(sprintf("  p-value:        %.4f\n", p))
#>   p-value:        0.0011
Show code 
cat("\nOn the adverse scale, OR > 1 indicates the treatment raises the odds of\n")
#> 
#> On the adverse scale, OR > 1 indicates the treatment raises the odds of
Show code 
cat("no improvement (harm); OR < 1 indicates fewer non-improvers (benefit).\n")
#> no improvement (harm); OR < 1 indicates fewer non-improvers (benefit).

4 Preliminary Analysis: Generalized Random Forests

Before running ForestSearch, we can use GRF to explore potential treatment effect heterogeneity and identify candidate factors. GRF runs here on the same adverse scale (y_binary_neg) with adverse_outcome = TRUE, so its risk-difference (RD) CATE is aligned with the harm direction used throughout.

Show code 
t0 <- proc.time()

grf_est <- grf.subg.harm.glm(
  data             = actg_df,
  confounders.name = confounders.name,
  outcome.name     = outcome.name,
  treat.name       = treat.name,
  id.name          = id.name,
  outcome_type     = fs_outcome_type,
  effect_measure   = fs_effect_measure,
  adverse_outcome  = TRUE,
  dmin.grf         = 0.05,     # RD-scale exploration floor (5 percentage points)
  maxdepth         = 2L,
  RCT              = TRUE,
  sg.criterion     = "mDiff",
  details          = TRUE
)

timings$grf <- (proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"]
Show code 
# leaf1 = recommend control, leaf2 = recommend treatment
if (!is.null(grf_est$trees)) {
  oldpar <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
  if (length(grf_est$trees) >= 1 && !is.null(grf_est$trees[[1]])) {
    plot(grf_est$trees[[1]], leaf.labels = c("Control", "Treat"), main = "Depth 1")
  }
  if (length(grf_est$trees) >= 2 && !is.null(grf_est$trees[[2]])) {
    plot(grf_est$trees[[2]], leaf.labels = c("Control", "Treat"), main = "Depth 2")
  }
  par(oldpar)
} else {
  cat("GRF: no policy trees available.\n")
}

GRF surfaces candidate factors driving treatment-effect heterogeneity on the adverse scale; ForestSearch then evaluates subgroup candidates with consistency filtering.

5 ForestSearch Analysis

5.1 Running ForestSearch

The selection engine for this main analysis is set by fs_subgroup_method in the setup chunk ("consistency", "dina", or "grf" with fs_grf_selection). Everything downstream — the full bootstrap, the Tier-2 de-biased gate, the cross-validation/leave-one-out diagnostics, and the subgroup outcome plot — runs off the single fitted object and therefore inherits that engine automatically, so the entire analysis re-renders under a different method by changing one knob. The consistency search (the default below) performs an exhaustive search over candidate subgroup combinations with up to maxk factors; the parameters in the table apply to that engine.

Parameter Value Description
effect_measure OR Odds ratio (binary)
effect.threshold 1.25 Screening OR threshold (adverse scale)
consistency.threshold 1.0 Per-split consistency OR threshold
pconsistency.threshold 0.90 Required consistency rate across splits
maxk 2 Maximum factors per subgroup
n.min 60 Minimum subgroup size
d0.min, d1.min 10 Minimum sample size per arm
consistency_method resample Required for the Tier-2 gate (GLM path)
Note

API note: GLM-natural vocabulary. This template uses the GLM-natural parameter names: sg_focus = "effMaxSG" (alias for the legacy "hrMaxSG"), effect.threshold (alias for hr.threshold), and consistency.threshold (alias for hr.consistency). The "eff*" and effect.* forms read more naturally for GLM outcomes (continuous MD, binary OR/RR/RD, count IRR) where there is no hazard ratio. The legacy "hr*" and hr.* forms continue to work and produce identical results. See NEWS.md for the full list of aliases.

NoteSelection criteria (sg_focus)

sg_focus controls which candidate subgroup is chosen once consistency has been evaluated. The example below uses "effMaxSG" with selection_rule = "both": the rule selects from the intersection of the effect-size neighborhood (candidates within effect_neighborhood of the maximum effect) and the Pareto non-dominated set on (effect, N), then picks the largest-N candidate. For OR (ratio measure), the neighborhood test is applied on the natural OR scale.

Show code 
t0 <- proc.time()

fs <- forestsearch(
  # --- Required data + roles ----------------------------------------------
  df.analysis               = actg_df,
  confounders.name          = confounders.name,
  outcome.name              = outcome.name,
  event.name                = outcome.name,    # binary: outcome IS the event
  treat.name                = treat.name,
  id.name                   = id.name,
  is.RCT                    = TRUE,
  seedit                    = analysis_seed,
  # --- GLM parameters -----------------------------------------------------
  outcome_type              = fs_outcome_type,
  effect_measure            = fs_effect_measure,
  adverse_outcome           = TRUE,
  # --- Screening engines (candidate generation) ---------------------------
  use_lasso                 = FALSE,
  use_grf                   = FALSE,
  grf_depth                 = fs_grf_depth,
  dmin.grf                  = fs_dmin_grf,
  frac.tau                  = 0.80,
  vi.grf.min                = -0.2,
  return_selected_cuts_only = TRUE,
  tune_grf                  = FALSE,
  use_dina                  = FALSE,
  dina_args                 = fs_dina_args,
  # --- Candidate-cut construction -----------------------------------------
  cut_type                  = "default",
  cont.cutoff               = 4L,
  conf.cont_jcuts           = list(cd40 = 10, wtkg = 10),
  # --- Selection engine ---------------------------------------------------
  subgroup_method           = fs_subgroup_method,        # consistency | dina | grf
  grf_selection             = fs_grf_selection,          # used when subgroup_method = "grf"
  grf_select_statistic      = fs_grf_select_statistic,   # frontier only
  dina_select_statistic     = fs_dina_select_statistic,  # used when subgroup_method = "dina"
  sg_focus                  = fs_sg_focus,
  selection_rule            = fs_selection_rule,

  # --- Tier-2 de-biased gate ----------------------------------------------

  mr_inference_args          = list(draws = mr_draws,

  # --- Subgroup constraints -----------------------------------------------

  d0.min                    = 10L,
  d1.min                    = 10L,

  # --- Thresholds (OR scale) ----------------------------------------------

  consistency.threshold     = fs_or_consistency,
  pconsistency.threshold    = fs_pconsistency,
  consistency_method        = fs_consistency_method,   # "resample" (gate requires it)

  parallel_args = list(
    plan = "multisession",
    workers = n_cores,
    show_message = TRUE
  )
)

5.2.4 Selection Diagnostic: Pareto Frontier

Beyond the single subgroup chosen by sg_focus, it is often informative to inspect the Pareto frontier on (effect, N) — the set of candidate subgroups that are not dominated on both axes simultaneously. A candidate is dominated when another candidate has at least as large an effect and at least as large a sample size, with at least one strict inequality. Under effMaxSG with selection_rule = "both" the selected subgroup is typically a frontier member that also sits in the effect-size band; the frontier serves both as the selection geometry and as a diagnostic of the trade-off space.

For OR outcomes the effect axis is auto-rendered on log scale by plot_pareto_frontier() and pareto_frontier_table() (auto-detected from fs$effect_measure); the rendered values are on the natural OR scale.

Show code 
# 1. Compute the split-derived CIs once (the expensive step).
ci_tab <- compute_frontier_cis(
  fs,
  n_splits = frontier_params$n_splits,
  seed     = frontier_params$seed
)

# 2. Plot, with split-derived CI bars overlaid; same intervals as the table.
p_pareto <- plot_pareto_frontier(
  fs,
  ci_table  = ci_tab,
  show_band = TRUE,
  xlim      = frontier_params$xlim
)
print(p_pareto)
Show code 
# 3. Render the table.  Selected subgroup is highlighted and marked with ★.
pareto_frontier_table(
  fs,
  ci_table = ci_tab,
  digits   = frontier_params$digits
)

5.2.5 Selection Narrative

explain_pareto_selection() describes the chosen subgroup relative to the non-dominated alternatives on the frontier.

Show code 
cat(explain_pareto_selection(fs, ci_table = ci_tab))

Selection criterion. The configured criterion is largest-N within the effect-size band (sg_focus = “hrMaxSG”) under the effect-size neighborhood rule. The effect-size band requires odds ratio within 10% of the maximum on the frontier (i.e., odds ratio >= 3.226). Within the eligible set, ties on N are broken by Pcons, then by effect strength, then by parsimony (smaller K).

Selected subgroup. !{cd40 <= 380} AND !{wtkg <= 86} (odds ratio = 3.584, N = 72, Pcons = 0.990, K = 2). This is the largest-N candidate in the eligible set among non-dominated frontier candidates. The Naive 95% CI for the odds ratio on this subgroup is (1.352, 9.503).

Non-selected frontier candidates (ordered by closeness to winning):

  • !{cd40 <= 449} AND !{wtkg <= 78} (odds ratio = 2.525, N = 74, Pcons = 0.940, K = 2). fell outside the effect-size band (odds ratio = 2.525 below the floor); excluded before the N tiebreaker even applies.

  • !{cd40 <= 413} AND !{wtkg <= 81} (odds ratio = 2.415, N = 92, Pcons = 0.960, K = 2). fell outside the effect-size band (odds ratio = 2.415 below the floor); excluded before the N tiebreaker even applies.

  • !{cd40 <= 380} AND !{wtkg <= 81} (odds ratio = 1.927, N = 117, Pcons = 0.910, K = 2). fell outside the effect-size band (odds ratio = 1.927 below the floor); excluded before the N tiebreaker even applies.

5.2.6 Agreement with GRF

ForestSearch and GRF identify subgroups by different mechanisms — FS via exhaustive search with consistency filtering, GRF via causal forests plus policy trees — so agreement on subject-level membership provides an informal robustness check. compare_fs_subgroups() produces a publication-ready cross-tabulation plus Cohen’s kappa; it accepts forestsearch and GRF result objects directly, and handles non-detection (method identifies no subgroup) by assigning all subjects to the complement.

Show code 
sg_compare <- compare_fs_subgroups(
  fs1               = fs,
  fs2               = grf_est,
  label1            = "ForestSearch",
  label2            = "GRF Standalone",
  id.name           = id.name,
  subgroup_notation = "harm",
  title             = "FS vs GRF: Subgroup Membership Concordance",
  subtitle          = "ACTG175 observed data (binary OR, adverse scale)",
  font_size         = 13
)

6 Bootstrap Bias Correction

6.1 Rationale

GLM estimates from identified subgroups are upwardly biased due to the selection process (subgroups are selected because they show extreme effects). Bootstrap bias correction addresses this by:

  1. Resampling with replacement
  2. Re-running the entire ForestSearch algorithm
  3. Computing bias terms from bootstrap vs. observed estimates
  4. Applying infinitesimal jackknife variance estimation

6.2 Running Bootstrap Analysis

Show code 
t0 <- proc.time()

fs_bc <- forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture(
  fs.est = fs,
  nb_boots = NB,
  show_three = FALSE,
  details = FALSE,
  digits = construction_digits,
  parallel_args = list(
    plan = "multisession",
    workers = n_cores,
    show_message = TRUE
  )
)

6.4 Fast de-biased gate vs. full bootstrap

The Tier-2 de-biased gate is a fast multiplier-bootstrap approximation of the bootstrap bias-correction. It reuses per-candidate GLM influence (dfbeta) over the selection engine’s own candidate family — the enumerated consistency candidates, DINA’s qualifying cuts, or GRF’s DR-score frontier, depending on fs_subgroup_method — and re-selects under multiplier draws, so its selection-bias term mirrors the same search optimism the full bootstrap corrects — without re-running the search per resample. The table below compares the gate (computed inside the fit) against the full bootstrap from the previous section. The naive-OR row is a scale sanity check; agreement on the de-biased row is the Tier-2-vs-Tier-1 validation. By default the de-biased CI uses the same infinitesimal-jackknife variance as the full bootstrap (the ci_method = 'ij' default), so the de-biased row compares both point estimate and interval like-for-like. The gate de-biases both the selected subgroup and its complement, so both appear in the comparison and the table below.

Selected subgroup: !{cd40 <= 380} & !{wtkg <= 86} (complement = remaining subjects)

de-biased OR (95% CI) 1.795 (0.632, 5.095) 2.427 (0.803, 7.333)
complement naive OR (95% CI) 0.587 (0.454, 0.759) 0.587 (0.454, 0.758)
complement de-biased OR (95% CI) 0.616 (0.370, 1.027) 0.606 (0.411, 0.893)

Timing: Tier 1 bootstrap (1000 boots) 90.5 s (1.5 min); Tier 2 gate 10.87 s -> 8x faster (multiplier loop only; the full bootstrap scales with NB, the gate does not).

Gate mr_harm_confirmed = TRUE (de-biased OR 1.795 vs gate 1.00); selection bias 0.6922 (log-OR). De-biased CI: robust SE (IJ SE 0.532 vs robust SE 0.512, log-OR). Complement (n = 1011): naive OR 0.587 -> de-biased 0.616 (selection bias -0.0501, log-OR).

7 DINA-Based Subgroup Identification

DINA (Doubly-robust Identification of Non-Additive effects) screens and selects subgroups from an influence-function representation of the covariate-specific treatment effect, fit with cross-fitting. For a binary endpoint the DINA family is "binomial" and the effect is reported on the OR scale. It plugs into the ForestSearch workflow in three complementary ways, all configured to mirror the main analysis above (same confounders, harm threshold, minimum size n.min = 60, and sg_focus):

  • (A) ForestSearch using DINA for screening — DINA’s per-covariate frontier contributes candidate cuts to the screening pool; the consistency search still performs selection.
  • (B) Standalone DINA with parameters analogous to (A) — the same fit’s frontier (the candidates (A) screens) and its single selected subgroup via dina_subgroup().
  • (C) ForestSearch with subgroup_method = "dina" — subgroup selection is delegated to dina_subgroup(), then the standard ForestSearch bootstrap provides the selection bias-corrected OR estimate.
# Shared DINA *fit* settings (binary outcome => family mapped to "binomial").
# Selection parameters (sg_focus, or_threshold) live in the setup chunk under
# the fs_dina_* knobs so they can be tuned independently; (B) and (C) read them.
dina_seed   <- 8316951L
dina_nfolds <- 2L
# Harm/benefit floor on the natural-parameter (log-OR) link scale for the
# binomial family.
m_diff_dina <- log(fs_dina_or_threshold)

7.1 (A) ForestSearch Using DINA for Screening

Here ForestSearch is run as in the main analysis, but with use_dina = TRUE: DINA’s frontier cuts are merged into the candidate pool alongside the GRF and LASSO cuts. dina_args is a flat, fully-named list; in the screening role it supplies the DINA fit tuning (seed, n_folds) and the frontier controls (scope, max_per_covariate, max_subgroups). scope = "wide" casts a deliberately wide net — the consistency stage remains the gatekeeper. By default dina_args$selected_only = TRUE, so screening contributes the single cut dina_subgroup() would select — using this call’s sg_focus / selection_rule / effect_neighborhood / effect.threshold, i.e. the same cut subgroup_method = "dina" (C) chooses. Set dina_args$selected_only = FALSE to contribute the full frontier instead.

Show code 
t0 <- proc.time()

fs_dina_screen <- forestsearch(
  # --- Required data + roles ----------------------------------------------
  df.analysis               = actg_df,
  confounders.name          = confounders.name,
  outcome.name              = outcome.name,
  event.name                = outcome.name,
  treat.name                = treat.name,
  id.name                   = id.name,
  is.RCT                    = TRUE,
  seedit                    = analysis_seed,
  # --- GLM parameters -----------------------------------------------------
  outcome_type              = fs_outcome_type,
  effect_measure            = fs_effect_measure,
  adverse_outcome           = TRUE,
  # --- Screening engines: GRF + LASSO + DINA ------------------------------
  use_lasso                 = TRUE,
  use_grf                   = TRUE,
  grf_depth                 = 2L,
  dmin.grf                  = 0,
  frac.tau                  = 0.80,
  vi.grf.min                = -0.2,
  return_selected_cuts_only = TRUE,
  tune_grf                  = FALSE,
  use_dina                  = TRUE,
  dina_args = list(
    seed = dina_seed, n_folds = dina_nfolds,
    scope = "wide", max_per_covariate = 3L, max_subgroups = 10L,
    selected_only = dina_screen_selected_only
  ),
  # --- Candidate-cut construction -----------------------------------------
  cut_type                  = "default",
  cont.cutoff               = 4L,
  conf.cont_jcuts           = list(cd40 = 10, wtkg = 10),
  # --- Selection engine ---------------------------------------------------
  subgroup_method           = "consistency",
  sg_focus                  = dina_screen_sg_focus,
  selection_rule            = "neighborhood",
  effect_neighborhood       = 0.10,
  # --- Subgroup constraints -----------------------------------------------
  n.min                     = 60L,
  d0.min                    = 10L,
  d1.min                    = 10L,
  maxk                      = 2L,
  # --- Thresholds (OR scale) ----------------------------------------------
  effect.threshold          = dina_screen_or_threshold,
  consistency.threshold     = dina_screen_or_consistency,
  pconsistency.threshold    = fs_pconsistency,
  consistency_method        = fs_consistency_method,
  # --- Consistency search -------------------------------------------------
  fs.splits                 = 500L,
  use_twostage              = TRUE,
  # --- Output / diagnostics -----------------------------------------------
  show_candidate_summary    = TRUE,
  details                   = TRUE,
  quiet                     = FALSE,
  plot.sg                   = FALSE,
  # --- Parallel -----------------------------------------------------------
  parallel_args = list(
    plan = "multisession",
    workers = n_cores,
    show_message = TRUE
  )
)

7.2 (B) Standalone DINA

The same DINA fit, run outside ForestSearch. Its dina_frontier() output is the candidate set fed into screening in (A); its dina_subgroup() output is the single subgroup selected by DINA itself — the mechanism (C) uses internally. Parameters are analogous to (A): same confounders, harm floor m_diff = log(fs_dina_or_threshold), n_min = 60, and sg_focus.

Show code 
t0 <- proc.time()

# Standalone DINA -- dina(), dina_frontier(), dina_subgroup() -- on the numeric
# covariate frame (all candidates are numeric per `data-covariates`).
dina_fit <- dina(
  df         = actg_df,
  outcome    = outcome.name,
  treatment  = treat.name,
  covariates = confounders.name,
  family     = "binomial",     # binary outcome (no status column required)
  # ... forwarded to dina_fit():
  seed              = dina_seed,   # default NULL
  n_folds           = dina_nfolds, # default 2L
  propensity_method = "logistic",  # default "logistic"
  cross_fitting     = TRUE         # default TRUE
)

timings$dina_standalone <- (proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"]
cat("Standalone DINA fit complete (family = binomial).\n")
#> Standalone DINA fit complete (family = binomial).

7.2.1 DINA Frontier (Screening Candidates)

Show code 
dina_fr <- dina_frontier(
  fit               = dina_fit,
  df                = actg_df,
  covariates        = confounders.name,
  scope             = "wide",     # default "wide"; or "harm" (requires m_diff)
  m_diff            = NULL,        # default NULL (no effect floor under scope = "wide")
  n_min             = 60L,        # default 60L
  direction         = "both",     # default "both"; or "left" / "right"
  max_per_covariate = 3L,         # default 3L
  max_subgroups     = 10L,        # default 10L
  digits            = 3L          # default 3L
)

7.2.2 DINA-Selected Subgroup

Show code 
dina_sel <- dina_subgroup(
  fit                 = dina_fit,
  df                  = actg_df,
  covariates          = confounders.name,
  m_diff              = m_diff_dina,
  n_min               = 60L,            # default 60L
  direction           = "both",         # default "both"; or "left" / "right"
  sg_focus            = fs_dina_sg_focus,
  selection_rule      = "neighborhood", # default "neighborhood"; pareto/both
  effect_neighborhood = 0.10,           # default 0.10
  alpha               = 0.05            # default 0.05
)

if (isTRUE(dina_sel$found)) {
  op <- if (identical(dina_sel$direction, "left")) "<=" else ">="
  cat(sprintf("DINA-selected subgroup: %s %s %s\n",
              dina_sel$covariate, op, format(dina_sel$threshold)))
  cat(sprintf("Direction: %s | N = %d\n",
              dina_sel$direction, dina_sel$n_subgroup))
} else {
  cat("Standalone DINA selected no subgroup meeting the criteria.\n")
}
#> DINA-selected subgroup: cd40 >= 500
#>  DINA-selected subgroup: drugs >=   0
#> Direction: right | N = 100
#>  Direction: left | N = 100

7.3 (C) ForestSearch with subgroup_method = "dina"

In this mode ForestSearch delegates subgroup selection to dina_subgroup(), bypassing GRF, LASSO and the consistency search. The selection criteria are inherited from this call’s sg_focus, n.min and effect.threshold (mapped to the log-OR harm floor); dina_args supplies only the fit tuning. The returned object is a standard forestsearch result, so the existing bootstrap machinery applies unchanged.

Show code 
t0 <- proc.time()

fs_dina <- forestsearch(
  # --- Required data + roles ----------------------------------------------
  df.analysis         = actg_df,
  confounders.name    = confounders.name,
  outcome.name        = outcome.name,
  event.name          = outcome.name,
  treat.name          = treat.name,
  id.name             = id.name,
  is.RCT              = TRUE,
  seedit              = analysis_seed,
  # --- GLM parameters -----------------------------------------------------
  outcome_type        = fs_outcome_type,
  effect_measure      = fs_effect_measure,
  adverse_outcome     = TRUE,
  # --- DINA-selection mode ------------------------------------------------
  subgroup_method     = "dina",
  dina_args           = list(seed = dina_seed, n_folds = dina_nfolds),  # fit tuning only
  dina_select_statistic = fs_dina_select_statistic,
  # --- Selection criteria (passed through to dina_subgroup) ---------------
  sg_focus            = fs_dina_sg_focus,
  selection_rule      = "neighborhood",

7.3.1 Bootstrap Bias-Corrected OR Estimates

The within-subgroup OR is upwardly biased by selection. The ForestSearch bootstrap corrects this by re-running the full pipeline on each resample; because the result above was produced in DINA-selection mode, each replicate re-fits DINA and re-runs dina_subgroup() from scratch — so the correction reflects the DINA selection process itself.

Show code 
# Runs only when DINA identified a subgroup.  The bootstrap bias-corrects an
# identified subgroup's effect, so there is nothing to do otherwise.
t0 <- proc.time()

fs_dina_bc <- forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture(
  fs.est = fs_dina,
  nb_boots = NB,
  show_three = FALSE,
  details = FALSE,
  digits = construction_digits,
  parallel_args = list(
    plan = "multisession",
    workers = n_cores,
    show_message = TRUE
  )
)

7.3.1.1 Tier-2 de-biased gate (counterpart to the Tier-1 bootstrap)

The same Tier-2-vs-Tier-1 comparison as the main analysis, for the DINA-selection fit. The gate de-biases against DINA’s own qualifying candidate family (re-running nothing), while the bootstrap above re-runs DINA on every resample.

For DINA the two tiers are not expected to agree as tightly as for the consistency method. DINA selects on its model-based tau-hat, but the gate can only re-select on the perturbed GLM OR; over a large depth-2 candidate family the gate’s winner’s-curse term can therefore exceed the bootstrap’s and over-correct the selected subgroup. To keep the gate’s re-selection neighbourhood close to DINA’s own selection band, the gate by default restricts that family to candidates competitive on DINA’s native tau-hat, matching the band to effect_neighborhood (the recommended default, used here via fs_dina_family_native_nbhd <- NULL; set an explicit number for a different band, or >= 1 to de-bias against the full unrestricted family). The complement is the induced residual rather than a max-over-family selection, so it agrees across tiers regardless. This band tunes only the candidate-competition part of the bias — the gate holds the DINA fit fixed, so the refit optimism is invisible to it; treat the full bootstrap as the reference for DINA and the gate as a fast, conservative check.

The Tier-1 bias-corrected table above, rebuilt from the Tier-2 gate object (the descriptive columns and naive effect are tier-independent; the bias-corrected column carries the gate’s de-biased estimate for the subgroup and its complement).

2 Bias-corrected OR: Bootstrap-adjusted estimate using infinitesimal jackknife method (5000 iterations). Corrects for optimism in subgroup selection.
3 Identified subgroup: {preanti >= 849.40000000000009} & {cd40 >= 338}
Note: RateC = control arm event rate; RateT = treatment arm event rate.
NoteScreening vs. selection roles for DINA

dina_args behaves differently by role. In the screening path (A, use_dina = TRUE) it defaults to selected_only = TRUE: the screening path calls dina_subgroup() and contributes only its selected cut, so it does consult this call’s sg_focus / selection_rule / effect_neighborhood — yielding the same cut the selection path (C) would choose. Setting selected_only = FALSE instead drives dina_frontier(), which is selection-agnostic and contributes the full candidate set. In the selection path (C, subgroup_method = "dina") the selection is always driven by this call’s sg_focus / selection_rule / effect_neighborhood via dina_subgroup(), and dina_args supplies only the fit. This mode is currently depth-1 (a single covariate threshold).

7.4 (D) ForestSearch with subgroup_method = "grf"

In this mode ForestSearch delegates subgroup selection to GRF — a causal-forest policy tree (grf_selection = "tree") or the doubly-robust-score frontier ("frontier") — bypassing LASSO, DINA and the consistency search. The selection criteria are inherited from this call’s sg_focus (mapped to the GRF frontier/tree rule), n.min, grf_depth, grf_selection and the DR-score harm floor dmin.grf (on the RD scale for binary). The returned object is a standard forestsearch result, so the existing bootstrap machinery applies unchanged.

Show code 
t0 <- proc.time()

fs_grf <- forestsearch(
  # --- Required data + roles ----------------------------------------------
  df.analysis         = actg_df,
  confounders.name    = confounders.name,
  outcome.name        = outcome.name,
  event.name          = outcome.name,
  treat.name          = treat.name,
  id.name             = id.name,
  is.RCT              = TRUE,
  seedit              = analysis_seed,   # also seeds the forest
  # --- GLM parameters -----------------------------------------------------
  outcome_type        = fs_outcome_type,
  effect_measure      = fs_effect_measure,
  adverse_outcome     = TRUE,
  # --- GRF-selection mode -------------------------------------------------
  subgroup_method     = "grf",
  grf_selection       = fs_grf_demo_selection,   # "tree" | "frontier"
  grf_select_statistic = fs_grf_select_statistic, # frontier only
  grf_depth           = fs_grf_demo_depth,
  dmin.grf            = fs_grf_demo_dmin,          # DR-score harm floor (RD scale)
  frac.tau            = 0.8,
  # --- Selection criteria -------------------------------------------------
  sg_focus            = fs_grf_sg_focus,          # -> GRF frontier/tree rule
  selection_rule      = "neighborhood",
  effect_neighborhood = 0.10,
  n.min               = 60L,
  # --- Tier-2 de-biased gate ----------------------------------------------
  mr_inference         = run_mr,
  mr_inference_args    = list(draws = mr_draws,
                             family_native_neighborhood = fs_grf_family_native_nbhd),
  # --- Output -------------------------------------------------------------
  details             = TRUE
  # NOTE: subgroup_method = "grf" bypasses LASSO, DINA and the consistency
  # search; use_lasso / use_dina / use_twostage / fs.splits / maxk and related
  # parameters do not apply in this mode.
)

7.4.1 Bootstrap Bias-Corrected OR Estimates

The within-subgroup OR is upwardly biased by selection. The ForestSearch bootstrap corrects this by re-running the full pipeline on each resample; because the result above was produced in GRF-selection mode, each replicate re-fits the causal forest and re-runs GRF selection from scratch — so the correction reflects the GRF selection process itself.

Show code

  nb_boots = NB,
  show_three = FALSE,
  details = FALSE,
  digits = construction_digits,
  parallel_args = list(
    plan = "multisession",
    workers = n_cores,
    show_message = TRUE
  )
)

7.4.1.1 Tier-2 de-biased gate (counterpart to the Tier-1 bootstrap)

The same Tier-2-vs-Tier-1 comparison as the main analysis, for the GRF-selection fit. The gate de-biases against GRF’s own DR-score candidate family (re-running nothing), while the bootstrap above re-runs GRF on every resample.

As with DINA, the two tiers are not expected to agree as tightly as for the consistency method. GRF selects on its doubly-robust (RD-based) score, but the gate can only re-select on the perturbed GLM OR; the additive RD scale and the multiplicative odds scale need not rank candidates the same way, so over a large candidate family the gate’s winner’s-curse term can exceed the bootstrap’s and over-correct the selected subgroup. To keep the gate’s re-selection neighbourhood close to GRF’s own selection band, the gate by default restricts that family to candidates competitive on GRF’s native DR-score, matching the band to effect_neighborhood (the recommended default, used here via fs_grf_family_native_nbhd <- NULL; set an explicit number for a different band, or >= 1 to de-bias against the full family). The complement is the induced residual rather than a max-over-family selection, so it agrees across tiers regardless. Two caveats specific to GRF: a dominant DR-score winner can collapse the restricted family to a single candidate (candidate family = 1 in the note below), in which case the gate removes only the gate-threshold optimism; and, more fundamentally, the band tunes only the candidate-competition part of the bias — the gate holds the causal forest fixed, so the forest-refit optimism that the bootstrap captures is invisible to it. Treat the full bootstrap as the reference for GRF and the gate as a fast, conservative check.

NoteSelection statistic vs. the gate’s re-selection (GRF)

GRF ranks candidates by the doubly-robust score (RD-based for binary), while the Tier-2 gate re-selects on the perturbed GLM OR. The two scales (additive RD vs. multiplicative odds) need not agree, so the gate is a proxy for GRF’s selection — the same approximation noted for DINA’s tau-hat. family_native_neighborhood restricts the gate family to DR-score-competitive candidates to keep that proxy close to GRF’s actual selection neighbourhood; the full bootstrap remains the reference because it re-runs the DR-score selection itself.

10.2 Interpretation Notes

The ForestSearch analysis identifies a subgroup where the treatment is associated with elevated odds of no CD4 improvement (harm on the adverse scale). As an exploratory result it requires the usual caveats:

  1. This is an exploratory analysis requiring independent validation.
  2. The bias-corrected (Tier-1 bootstrap and Tier-2 gate) estimates have wider confidence intervals than the naive subgroup OR.
  3. Cross-validation metrics should be evaluated for algorithm stability.

The Tier-1/Tier-2 comparison is the methodological focus: for the consistency engine the gate is expected to track the full bootstrap closely on both point estimate and IJ interval; for DINA and GRF the gate is a fast, conservative proxy (it holds the engine’s fit fixed), so the full bootstrap remains the reference.

> **Method-general analysis.** The selection engine for the main analysis is set
> once via `fs_subgroup_method` in the setup chunk — `"consistency"` (default),
> `"dina"`, or `"grf"` (with `fs_grf_selection` = `"tree"`/`"frontier"`). The
> headline fit and every downstream step — full bootstrap, Tier-2 de-biased gate,
> cross-validation, leave-one-out, and the subgroup outcome plot — inherit that
> engine from the single fitted object, so the whole analysis re-renders under a
> different method by changing one knob. The comparative DINA-screening,
> standalone-DINA, and GRF sections that follow are fixed illustrations of the
> individual engines and are unaffected by `fs_subgroup_method`.
>
> This is the **binary-outcome (odds-ratio) counterpart** to the GBSG Cox
> multimethod vignette. Everything operates on a single **adverse scale**
> (`y_binary_neg`, the indicator of *no* CD4 improvement), so an OR above the
> screening threshold indicates harm — the direct analogue of an HR above the
> threshold on the survival path. The Tier-1 (full bootstrap) vs Tier-2 (fast
> multiplier-bootstrap de-biased gate) comparison is reported for each engine.

## Parallel Processing Configuration

ForestSearch supports parallel processing for computationally intensive
operations (bootstrap, cross-validation).

```{r parallel-setup}
# Detect available cores
n_cores_total <- parallel::detectCores()
n_cores <- max(1L, floor(0.80 * parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE)))
cat("Using", n_cores, "of", n_cores_total, "total cores for parallel processing")

# Number of bootstrap iterations
# Use 500-2000 for production; reduced here for demo / pressure test
NB <- 1000L

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Validation toggles (the slowest parts of the document).  Independent:
# run_cv  controls K-Fold cross-validation; run_loo controls leave-one-out
# (N-fold / OOB).  Either can be turned off without affecting the other.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
run_cv  <- FALSE    # K-Fold cross-validation (kfold-cv + diagnostics)
run_loo <- FALSE    # Leave-one-out / N-fold OOB (oob-cv)
# 10-fold CV with multiple iterations.  Use Ksims >= 50 for production.
Ksims <- 50L

# Pre-seed CV/LOO timings so the Computational Timing table is well-formed
# whether or not these run (skipped analyses report NA).
timings$kfold <- NA_real_
timings$oob   <- NA_real_

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Per-analysis identification parameters (tune each analysis independently).
#   sg_focus       : which candidate subgroup the selection step chooses
#   or_threshold   : harm floor on the OR scale (adverse scale: OR > c1 = harm)
#   or_consistency : minimum per-split consistency OR (consistency search only)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main ForestSearch (consistency search)
fs_sg_focus              <- "effMaxSG"   # GLM-natural alias of "hrMaxSG"
fs_selection_rule        <- "neighborhood"       # neighborhood ∩ Pareto (effMaxSG/effMinSG)
fs_or_threshold          <- 1.0
fs_or_consistency        <- 1.0
fs_pconsistency          <- 0.90
# IMPORTANT: the Tier-2 de-biased gate on the GLM path runs ONLY under the
# resample-consistency engine (consistency_method = "resample").  Under the
# default "split" engine the gate is silently skipped for GLM outcomes.
fs_consistency_method    <- "resample"
# Tier-2 de-biased gate: a fast multiplier-bootstrap approximation of the
# bootstrap bias-correction, computed inside the fit and compared to the full
# bootstrap below.  It runs for whichever selection engine fs_subgroup_method
# names, de-biasing against that engine's own candidate family (it re-derives
# the per-candidate GLM dfbeta itself).
run_mr <- TRUE     # add mr_inference = TRUE to the forestsearch call
mr_draws      <- 5000L    # multiplier-bootstrap draws for the gate

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output location for this document's results:  <base>/<dirout>/
#   results_dir = NULL -> base is <qmd dir>/_payloads
#   dirout      = NULL -> the .qmd stem
# Setting results_dir redirects the base only; each run still gets its own
# subdirectory named by dirout.
#
# Examples:
#   results_dir <- NULL;  dirout <- NULL
#     -> <qmd dir>/_payloads/<stem>/<stem>_payload.rds
#   results_dir <- NULL;  dirout <- "gbsg_survival_multimethod"
#     -> <qmd dir>/_payloads/gbsg_survival_multimethod/gbsg_survival_multimethod_payload.rds
#   results_dir <- "~/GitHub/fs-post-selection-manuscript_jasa/_payloads"; dirout <- NULL
#     -> ~/GitHub/fs-post-selection-manuscript_jasa/_payloads/<stem>/<stem>_payload.rds
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
results_dir <- NULL
dirout      <- NULL

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# FIXED-FAMILY CONFIGURATION (use_lasso = FALSE, use_grf = FALSE)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fully enumerated candidate family: no LASSO or GRF screening, and as of
# 2026-08 no max_subgroups_search truncation.
#
# This is the fixed-family configuration the method's Theorem 1 certifies:
# the family is enumerated (default cuts, with J = 10 cuts for wtkg and
# cd40) rather than model-screened, so the bias correction captures all
# selection optimism.
#
# The published supplement Table S11 ({wtkg>86} & {cd40>380}, n=72,
# naive OR 3.58, FB 2.43, MR 1.80) came from an earlier run of this document
# that capped candidate evaluation at 50 (max_subgroups_search = 50L). That
# cap has been removed so the analysis follows the recommended specification
# rather than the earlier run. Results may therefore differ from the
# published table; the difference is intentional.
#
# Prior run (superseded): payload built 2026-07-08 on the 128-core machine,
# 5000 MR draws, max_subgroups_search = 50L.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Selection engine for the MAIN analysis.  The headline fit, its bootstrap,
# the de-biased gate, CV/LOO, and the subgroup outcome plot all flow from this
# single fit, so flipping subgroup_method re-runs the entire main analysis
# under that engine (each downstream step inherits the method from the fitted
# object):
#   "consistency" - the splitting-consistency search (default);
#   "dina"        - DINA performs selection (consistency search bypassed);
#   "grf"         - GRF performs selection (policy tree or DR-frontier).
# The Tier-2 gate de-biases against whichever engine's OWN candidate family,
# with re-selection matching that engine's selection rule.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
fs_subgroup_method <- "consistency"  # "consistency" | "dina" | "grf"
fs_grf_selection   <- "frontier"     # only if subgroup_method == "grf": "tree" | "frontier"
fs_grf_select_statistic <- "effect"  # only if subgroup_method=="grf" & grf_selection=="frontier": "dr" | "effect".
                                     #   "dr"     = native DR-score frontier winner;
                                     #   "effect" = re-rank the DR frontier on the inferential GLM OR (the
                                     #              statistic the Tier-2 gate de-biases).  No-op for the policy tree.
fs_grf_depth       <- 2L             # GRF depth (screening + GRF selection)
fs_dmin_grf        <- 0              # GRF DR-score screening floor (RD scale for binary; 0 = permissive)
fs_dina_args       <- list()         # extra args forwarded to DINA selection
fs_dina_select_statistic <- "effect" # only if subgroup_method=="dina": "dina" | "effect".
                                     #   "dina"   = native DINA tau-hat winner;
                                     #   "effect" = re-rank the DINA family on the inferential GLM OR (the
                                     #              statistic the Tier-2 gate de-biases).
# Tier-2 gate (main analysis): the gate's re-selection family for "dina"/"grf" is
# restricted to candidates competitive on the method's NATIVE statistic (DINA
# tau-hat / GRF DR-score).  NULL = use the recommended default, which matches the
# band to effect_neighborhood automatically (the band the engine selects within);
# give a number in (0, 1) to set the band explicitly, or >= 1 to de-bias against
# the full family.  Ignored for "consistency" (its maxcons re-selection already
# matches the search).
fs_family_native_nbhd <- NULL

# (A) ForestSearch + DINA screening (consistency search selects; DINA only
#     contributes candidate cuts)
dina_screen_sg_focus             <- "effMaxSG"
dina_screen_or_threshold         <- 1.0
dina_screen_or_consistency       <- 0.9
# Screening cut set: FALSE => full DINA frontier; TRUE => only the single
# dina_subgroup()-selected cut (uses dina_screen_sg_focus / selection_rule).
dina_screen_selected_only        <- TRUE

# (C) ForestSearch subgroup_method = "dina" (DINA performs selection; the
#     consistency search is bypassed, so or_consistency does not apply here).
#     The standalone DINA analysis (B) reuses these so (B) and (C) match.
fs_dina_sg_focus     <- "effMaxSG"
fs_dina_or_threshold <- 1.0
# Tier-2 gate: the DINA re-selection family is restricted to candidates competitive
# on DINA's native tau-hat.  NULL = recommended default (matches effect_neighborhood
# automatically); set a number in (0, 1) for an explicit band, or >= 1 for the full
# family.  Note: this only tunes candidate competition -- the gate holds the forest
# fixed, so the full bootstrap stays the reference for DINA regardless.
fs_dina_family_native_nbhd <- NULL

# (D) ForestSearch subgroup_method = "grf" (GRF performs selection via a causal
#     forest policy tree or DR-score frontier; the consistency search, LASSO and
#     DINA are bypassed).  Dedicated demo: always runs GRF regardless of
#     fs_subgroup_method, mirroring the standalone DINA selection (C).
fs_grf_demo_selection     <- "frontier"  # "frontier" | "tree"
fs_grf_demo_depth         <- 2L          # GRF tree / DR-pair depth
fs_grf_demo_dmin          <- 0.0         # DR-score harm floor (RD scale; 0 = permissive default)
fs_grf_sg_focus           <- "effMaxSG"  # -> GRF frontier/tree selection rule
# Tier-2 gate: the GRF re-selection family is restricted to candidates competitive
# on GRF's native (RD-based) DR-score.  NULL = recommended default (matches
# effect_neighborhood automatically); set a number in (0, 1) for an explicit band,
# or >= 1 for the full family.  Note: this only tunes candidate competition -- the
# gate holds the forest fixed, so the full bootstrap stays the reference for GRF
# regardless (a dominant DR-score winner can collapse the family to 1).
fs_grf_family_native_nbhd <- NULL

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Numeric precision (two-stage control).
#   construction_digits : upstream sprintf precision in the bootstrap / CV
#     table builders.  Acts as a CEILING for downstream display.
#   display_digits      : precision rendered in user-facing tables.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
construction_digits <- 2L
display_digits      <- 2L

# Display-only tidy of a subgroup label for printing: rounds the post-operator
# thresholds to `d` decimals via the package's tidy_cut_display().  The
# membership-exact sg.harm (re-parsed by get_dfpred and carried through the
# bootstrap) is never altered -- this only affects what is printed.  Used at
# every site in this document that renders sg.harm.
fmt_sg <- function(x, d = display_digits) {
  if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0L) return(x)
  paste(forestsearch:::tidy_cut_display(x, digits = as.integer(d)), collapse = " & ")
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pareto-frontier diagnostic parameters (drives compute_frontier_cis(),
# plot_pareto_frontier(), pareto_frontier_table(), explain_pareto_selection()).
# For OR (ratio-scale), the effect axis is auto-rendered on log scale.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
frontier_params <- list(
  n_splits      = 1000L,
  seed          = 1L,
  xlim          = c(0.35, 10),   # OR auto-detected as ratio scale
  digits        = 2L
)
```



# Introduction

This vignette demonstrates the **ForestSearch** methodology for exploratory
subgroup identification with a **binary outcome on the odds-ratio (OR) scale**,
applied to the ACTG175 trial. It uses the GLM extension of ForestSearch
(León et al. 2024 *Statistics in Medicine*) and is the binary-outcome
counterpart to the GBSG Cox multimethod analysis.

## Motivation

In clinical trials, particularly oncology and infectious-disease studies,
subgroup analyses are essential for:

- Evaluating treatment effect consistency across patient populations
- Identifying subgroups where treatment may be detrimental (harm)
- Characterizing subgroups with enhanced benefit
- Informing regulatory decisions and clinical practice

While prespecified subgroups provide stronger evidence, important subgroups
based on patient characteristics may not be anticipated. ForestSearch provides
a principled approach to **exploratory** subgroup identification with proper
statistical inference.

## Methodology Overview

ForestSearch identifies subgroups through:

1. **Candidate factor selection**: Using LASSO and/or Generalized Random Forests (GRF)
2. **Exhaustive subgroup search**: Evaluating all combinations up to `maxk` factors
3. **Consistency-based selection**: Applying splitting consistency criteria
4. **Bootstrap bias correction**: Adjusting for selection-induced optimism
5. **Cross-validation**: Assessing algorithm stability

The key innovation is the **splitting consistency criterion**: a subgroup is
considered "consistent with harm" if, when randomly split 50/50 many times,
both halves consistently show odds ratios at or above the harm threshold (for
example, 1.0 representing a nominal "harm" boundary on the adverse scale).

## Single-Scale (Adverse) Framing

::: {.callout-note}
**ForestSearch and threshold direction.** ForestSearch was developed for
survival data where the outcome is typically the timing of an adverse event and
thresholds (e.g., indicative of harm) are defined on the hazard-ratio scale.
For a binary endpoint, the same harm logic applies on the **adverse scale**: the
outcome `y_binary_neg = 1 - y_binary_pos` is the indicator of *no* CD4
improvement (1 = worse), and with `adverse_outcome = TRUE` an OR above the
screening threshold means the treatment **increases the odds of no improvement**
(harm). This is the direct binary analogue of an HR above the threshold on the
survival path, so the entire multimethod workflow — consistency, DINA, and GRF —
runs on this one scale.
:::

## Trial Background

ACTG175 (Hammer et al. 1996) randomized HIV-positive patients with CD4
counts of 200–500 per mm³ to four treatment arms. This analysis uses the
two pure-monotherapy/combination arms:

- **Arm 1**: ZDV + ddI combination therapy (treatment, T = 1)
- **Arm 3**: ddI monotherapy (control, T = 0)

The outcome is the change in CD4 count from baseline to week 20 (`cd40` →
`cd420`), dichotomized into the improvement indicator.


# Setup

## Load Required Packages

```{r load-packages}
#| code-fold: false
library(forestsearch)
library(speff2trial)
library(survival)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(gt)
library(grf)
library(policytree)
library(doFuture)
library(future)

# Optional packages for enhanced output
library(patchwork)
library(forestploter)

# Set ggplot theme
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
```

## Confounders and Variable Roles

```{r analysis-roles}
#| code-fold: false

# ─── Reproducibility ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
analysis_seed <- 8316951L
set.seed(analysis_seed)

# ─── Confounders ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cont_vars <- c("age", "preanti", "wtkg", "karnof", "cd40", "cd80")
bin_vars  <- c("hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom")
confounders.name <- c(cont_vars, bin_vars)
id.name   <- "id"

# ─── Variables (single adverse scale) ──────────────────────────────────
treat.name   <- "treat"
outcome.name <- "y_binary_neg"   # FS adverse-scale outcome (1 = no improvement)

# ─── ForestSearch GLM parameters (binary, OR scale) ────────────────────
fs_outcome_type   <- "binary"
fs_effect_measure <- "OR"
```


# Data: ACTG175 Trial

## Treatment Assignment

```{r data-treat}
# ACTG175: arm 1 = ZDV+ddI (experimental), arm 3 = ddI (control)
actg_df <- subset(speff2trial::ACTG175, arms %in% c(1L, 3L))
actg_df$id <- seq_len(nrow(actg_df))

# Treatment: ZDV+ddI = 1, ddI = 0 (no switching)
actg_df$treat <- ifelse(actg_df$arms == 1L, 1L, 0L)
```

## Outcome Construction

```{r data-outcomes}
# Drop subjects missing the week-20 CD4 measurement
actg_df <- actg_df[!is.na(actg_df$cd420), ]

# Beneficial scale: CD4 improvement indicator (1 = improved, higher = better)
actg_df$y_binary_pos <- as.integer(actg_df$cd420 > actg_df$cd40)

# Adverse scale: NO improvement indicator (1 = did not improve, higher = worse).
# This is the single analysis scale for the entire multimethod workflow.
actg_df$y_binary_neg <- 1L - actg_df$y_binary_pos

cat("Sample size:", nrow(actg_df), "\n")
cat("Adverse events (no improvement):", sum(actg_df$y_binary_neg),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * mean(actg_df$y_binary_neg)))
cat("Baseline factors:", paste(confounders.name, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## Covariates

```{r data-covariates}
# Keep ALL candidate covariates numeric.  forestsearch() builds and evaluates
# "var <= value" candidate cuts, and its DINA paths require numeric columns, so
# binary indicators left as factors trigger hundreds of "'<=' not meaningful for
# factors" warnings during the consistency search and "covariate must be numeric"
# failures in DINA (both subgroup_method = "dina" selection and use_dina
# screening).  With 0/1 numeric coding, forestsearch's cont.cutoff (= 4 unique
# values) treats the binary candidates as categorical automatically -- no factor
# conversion is needed, and every engine (consistency, DINA, GRF, standalone
# DINA) receives numeric covariates.
for (v in bin_vars) actg_df[[v]] <- as.numeric(actg_df[[v]])

cat("Continuous candidates:", paste(cont_vars, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Binary candidates:    ", paste(bin_vars, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## Baseline Characteristics

```{r baseline-table}
create_summary_table(
  data = actg_df,
  treat_var = treat.name,
  table_title = "ACTG175 Baseline Characteristics and Outcome by Treatment Arm",
  vars_continuous = c("y_binary_neg", cont_vars),
  vars_categorical = bin_vars,
  font_size = 12
)
```

## ITT Analysis (Adverse Scale)

```{r itt-analysis}
# Adverse-scale ITT OR (y_binary_neg = no improvement; OR > 1 = treatment
# increases the odds of no improvement = harm).
itt_neg <- glm(y_binary_neg ~ treat, data = actg_df, family = binomial)

beta  <- coef(itt_neg)["treat"]
se    <- summary(itt_neg)$coefficients["treat", "Std. Error"]
z     <- beta / se
p     <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(z))
itt_or    <- exp(beta)
itt_ci_lo <- exp(beta - qnorm(0.975) * se)
itt_ci_hi <- exp(beta + qnorm(0.975) * se)

cat("=== ITT Odds Ratio, adverse scale (y_binary_neg) ===\n")
cat(sprintf("  log-OR (treat): %7.4f  (SE %.4f)\n", beta, se))
cat(sprintf("  OR:             %6.3f  (95%% CI: %.3f, %.3f)\n",
            itt_or, itt_ci_lo, itt_ci_hi))
cat(sprintf("  p-value:        %.4f\n", p))
cat("\nOn the adverse scale, OR > 1 indicates the treatment raises the odds of\n")
cat("no improvement (harm); OR < 1 indicates fewer non-improvers (benefit).\n")
```


# Preliminary Analysis: Generalized Random Forests

Before running ForestSearch, we can use GRF to explore potential treatment
effect heterogeneity and identify candidate factors. GRF runs here on the same
adverse scale (`y_binary_neg`) with `adverse_outcome = TRUE`, so its
risk-difference (RD) CATE is aligned with the harm direction used throughout.

```{r grf-analysis}
t0 <- proc.time()

grf_est <- grf.subg.harm.glm(
  data             = actg_df,
  confounders.name = confounders.name,
  outcome.name     = outcome.name,
  treat.name       = treat.name,
  id.name          = id.name,
  outcome_type     = fs_outcome_type,
  effect_measure   = fs_effect_measure,
  adverse_outcome  = TRUE,
  dmin.grf         = 0.05,     # RD-scale exploration floor (5 percentage points)
  maxdepth         = 2L,
  RCT              = TRUE,
  sg.criterion     = "mDiff",
  details          = TRUE
)

timings$grf <- (proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"]
```

```{r grf-trees}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Policy trees from GRF (depth 1 and 2), adverse scale"

# leaf1 = recommend control, leaf2 = recommend treatment
if (!is.null(grf_est$trees)) {
  oldpar <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
  if (length(grf_est$trees) >= 1 && !is.null(grf_est$trees[[1]])) {
    plot(grf_est$trees[[1]], leaf.labels = c("Control", "Treat"), main = "Depth 1")
  }
  if (length(grf_est$trees) >= 2 && !is.null(grf_est$trees[[2]])) {
    plot(grf_est$trees[[2]], leaf.labels = c("Control", "Treat"), main = "Depth 2")
  }
  par(oldpar)
} else {
  cat("GRF: no policy trees available.\n")
}
```

GRF surfaces candidate factors driving treatment-effect heterogeneity on the
adverse scale; ForestSearch then evaluates subgroup candidates with consistency
filtering.


# ForestSearch Analysis

## Running ForestSearch

The selection engine for this main analysis is set by `fs_subgroup_method` in
the setup chunk (`"consistency"`, `"dina"`, or `"grf"` with `fs_grf_selection`).
Everything downstream — the full bootstrap, the Tier-2 de-biased gate, the
cross-validation/leave-one-out diagnostics, and the subgroup outcome plot — runs
off the single fitted object and therefore inherits that engine automatically,
so the entire analysis re-renders under a different method by changing one knob.
The consistency search (the default below) performs an exhaustive search over
candidate subgroup combinations with up to `maxk` factors; the parameters in the
table apply to that engine.

| Parameter | Value | Description |
|-----------|-------|-------------|
| `effect_measure` | `OR` | Odds ratio (binary) |
| `effect.threshold` | 1.25 | Screening OR threshold (adverse scale) |
| `consistency.threshold` | 1.0 | Per-split consistency OR threshold |
| `pconsistency.threshold` | 0.90 | Required consistency rate across splits |
| `maxk` | 2 | Maximum factors per subgroup |
| `n.min` | 60 | Minimum subgroup size |
| `d0.min`, `d1.min` | 10 | Minimum sample size per arm |
| `consistency_method` | `resample` | Required for the Tier-2 gate (GLM path) |

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
**API note: GLM-natural vocabulary.** This template uses the GLM-natural
parameter names: `sg_focus = "effMaxSG"` (alias for the legacy `"hrMaxSG"`),
`effect.threshold` (alias for `hr.threshold`), and `consistency.threshold`
(alias for `hr.consistency`). The `"eff*"` and `effect.*` forms read more
naturally for GLM outcomes (continuous MD, binary OR/RR/RD, count IRR) where
there is no hazard ratio. The legacy `"hr*"` and `hr.*` forms continue to work
and produce identical results. See `NEWS.md` for the full list of aliases.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Selection criteria (`sg_focus`)

`sg_focus` controls which candidate subgroup is chosen once consistency has been
evaluated. The example below uses `"effMaxSG"` with `selection_rule = "both"`:
the rule selects from the **intersection** of the effect-size neighborhood
(candidates within `effect_neighborhood` of the maximum effect) and the Pareto
non-dominated set on (effect, N), then picks the largest-N candidate. For OR
(ratio measure), the neighborhood test is applied on the natural OR scale.
:::

```{r forestsearch-main}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7

t0 <- proc.time()

fs <- forestsearch(
  # --- Required data + roles ----------------------------------------------
  df.analysis               = actg_df,
  confounders.name          = confounders.name,
  outcome.name              = outcome.name,
  event.name                = outcome.name,    # binary: outcome IS the event
  treat.name                = treat.name,
  id.name                   = id.name,
  is.RCT                    = TRUE,
  seedit                    = analysis_seed,
  # --- GLM parameters -----------------------------------------------------
  outcome_type              = fs_outcome_type,
  effect_measure            = fs_effect_measure,
  adverse_outcome           = TRUE,
  # --- Screening engines (candidate generation) ---------------------------
  use_lasso                 = FALSE,
  use_grf                   = FALSE,
  grf_depth                 = fs_grf_depth,
  dmin.grf                  = fs_dmin_grf,
  frac.tau                  = 0.80,
  vi.grf.min                = -0.2,
  return_selected_cuts_only = TRUE,
  tune_grf                  = FALSE,
  use_dina                  = FALSE,
  dina_args                 = fs_dina_args,
  # --- Candidate-cut construction -----------------------------------------
  cut_type                  = "default",
  cont.cutoff               = 4L,
  conf.cont_jcuts           = list(cd40 = 10, wtkg = 10),
  # --- Selection engine ---------------------------------------------------
  subgroup_method           = fs_subgroup_method,        # consistency | dina | grf
  grf_selection             = fs_grf_selection,          # used when subgroup_method = "grf"
  grf_select_statistic      = fs_grf_select_statistic,   # frontier only
  dina_select_statistic     = fs_dina_select_statistic,  # used when subgroup_method = "dina"
  sg_focus                  = fs_sg_focus,
  selection_rule            = fs_selection_rule,
  effect_neighborhood       = 0.10,
  # --- Tier-2 de-biased gate ----------------------------------------------
  mr_inference               = run_mr,
  mr_inference_args          = list(draws = mr_draws,
                                   family_native_neighborhood = fs_family_native_nbhd),
  # --- Subgroup constraints -----------------------------------------------
  n.min                     = 60L,
  d0.min                    = 10L,
  d1.min                    = 10L,
  maxk                      = 2L,
  # --- Thresholds (OR scale) ----------------------------------------------
  effect.threshold          = fs_or_threshold,
  consistency.threshold     = fs_or_consistency,
  pconsistency.threshold    = fs_pconsistency,
  consistency_method        = fs_consistency_method,   # "resample" (gate requires it)
  # --- Consistency search -------------------------------------------------
  fs.splits                 = 500L,
  use_twostage              = TRUE,
  # --- Output / diagnostics -----------------------------------------------
  show_candidate_summary    = TRUE,
  details                   = TRUE,
  quiet                     = FALSE,
  plot.sg                   = FALSE,   # KM not applicable; use plot_sg_glm_outcomes()
  # --- Parallel -----------------------------------------------------------
  parallel_args = list(
    plan = "multisession",
    workers = n_cores,
    show_message = TRUE
  )
)

plan("sequential"); gc(verbose = FALSE)
timings$forestsearch <- (proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"]

cat("\nForestSearch completed in",
    round(timings$forestsearch, 1), "seconds\n")
```

  cat("Identified subgroup (H):", fmt_sg(fs$sg.harm), "\n")
